description: Introduce oneself (Je m'appelle…) and others; ask for names using tu (Comment tu t'appelles?) and vous (Comment vous vous appelez?); conjugate s'appeler across all persons; use M./Mme as forms of address
canDo: I can introduce myself and other people, ask someone their name, and address someone politely with M./Mme.
competence: Conjugate s'appeler in all 6 persons (≥5/6); ask a name with tu and with vous; introduce a third person (Il/Elle s'appelle…); use M./Mme as a form of address.

description: Distinguish and select tu, vous (singular polite), and vous (plural) across 12 social situations
canDo: I can tell which pronoun (tu vs vous) is more appropriate depending on whom I am addressing.
competence: Select tu / vous (polite sg) / vous (pl) correctly in ≥10/12 situations; give a one-phrase reason for each choice.

description: Name all 26 letters; group by vowel sound in name (ah: A H K · ay: B C D É G P T V W · air: È F L M N R S Z · i: I J X Y · ü: Q U · oh: O · uh: E); spell aloud: Comment ça s'écrit?
canDo: I can say how a name is spelled, or ask how it is spelled.
competence: Name all 26 letters; sort them into the 7 vowel-sound groups; spell a given word aloud (≥90% letters correct).

description: Name 7 days and 3 moments of the day (matin, après-midi, soir); ask/answer C'est quand?; weekday vs weekend
canDo: I can tell which day of the week and what moment of the day it is, or ask: When is it?
competence: List the 7 days in order and the 3 moments of the day; label a day as weekday/weekend; ask and answer C'est quand ?

description: Name 12 colours; associate each with a mnemonic object (le feu rouge, le flamant rose…)
canDo: I know the word for twelve different colors in French (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, brown, white, black, grey, pink, beige), or ask: How is it? (What color is it?)
competence: Name the 12 colours; give the matching mnemonic object for each (≥10/12).

description: Use C'est où ? / C'est qui ? / C'est quoi ? to identify people, places and things; 18 nouns whose meaning is already clear in English, so the new thing to learn is the gender: un homme, une femme, un étudiant, une étudiante, un groupe, une classe, un café, une région, une province, un sport, le football, une activité, la danse, un croissant, un macaron, le champagne, une consonne, une nationalité.
canDo: I can say whether a noun is masculine or feminine, and answer Where is it? Who is it? What is it? with it.
competence: Label the 18 nouns with un/une/le/la (≥15/18); answer C'est où ? / C'est qui ? / C'est quoi ? appropriately for a given item.

description: Read and say 0–16; recognise 17,18,19 as composites; say 20; respond to Il y a combien d'étudiants ?
canDo: I know my French numbers from 0 to 20, or ask how many students there are in the classroom.
competence: Read aloud any number 0–20; identify 17–19 as composites (dix-sept = 10 + 7); say 20; answer Il y a combien d'étudiants ?

description: Understand and respond to: Écoutez!, Regardez!, Répétez!, Lisez!, Écrivez!, Parlez!, Notez!, Comptez!, Associez!; ask On fait quoi?
canDo: I can understand and respond to classroom instructions like Écoutez !, Regardez !, Répétez !, Lisez !, Écrivez !, Parlez !, Notez !, Comptez !, Associez !, or ask what we are doing.
competence: Perform the correct action for the 9 instructions (≥8/9); ask On fait quoi ?

description: Greet and take leave; distinguish formal, versatile, and casual by time of day and register
canDo: I can greet and say goodbye based on time of day and register (casual or formal).
competence: Produce the register-appropriate greeting/leave-taking for a given time and relationship (≥8/10); sort phrases into meeting vs parting and universal vs familiar.

description: Simulate a first-time meeting in French with a fellow student (tu), a client (vous) or a group (plural vous), chaining greeting, asking a name, giving one's own, asking how it's spelled and taking leave: Bonjour → Comment tu t'appelles / vous vous appelez ? → Et toi ? / Et vous ? → Comment ça s'écrit ? → Enchanté(e) → Au revoir !
canDo: I can carry a first meeting in French right through, with a fellow student, with a client, or with a group.
competence: Complete every step — greet, ask a name, give one's own name, ask Et toi ? / Et vous ?, ask and answer Comment ça s'écrit ?, say Enchanté(e), take leave — in the register the situation calls for: tu, vous, or the plural vous of a group (≥6/7 steps in each of the 3).

description: Match subject pronoun → stressed pronoun (moi, toi, lui, elle, nous, vous, eux, elles); use ___, je… frame; sort into subject-only / stressed-only / either
canDo: I can identify any of the 8 stressed pronouns (moi, toi, lui, elle, nous, vous, eux, elles) by their position — after a preposition, after c'est, or standing alone (avec moi, c'est moi, moi !).
competence: Match each of them to their 8 subject pronouns (je, tu, …) (≥7/8).

description: Name 10 professions in m/f forms; use il est / elle est and C'est un/une ___
canDo: I can say what job someone has.
competence: Name 10 professions in m/f forms; present a person with il est/elle est or C'est un/une ___ (≥8/10).
fr: Tu fais quoi dans la vie ?

description: Name academic subjects with correct article; ask Qu'est-ce que tu étudies? / Je suis étudiant(e) en ___
canDo: I can say and ask what someone is studying.
competence: Name academic subjects with the correct article; answer Qu'est-ce que tu étudies ? with Je suis étudiant(e) en ___.

description: Conjugate être across 8 persons; m/f agreement (étudiant/étudiante, étudiants/étudiantes)
canDo: I can say who someone is and give basic information about people, making the form agree for gender and number.
competence: Conjugate être in all 8 persons (≥7/8); apply m/f and sg/pl agreement to étudiant(e)(s).
fr: Je suis, tu es, il est…

description: Name and identify 25 countries with correct article (le, la, l', les, ∅); ask C'est quel pays?
canDo: I can name countries with the correct article and ask which country something is.
competence: Label 25 countries with le/la/l'/les/∅ (≥20/25); ask C'est quel pays ?

description: Produce nationality adjectives in 4 forms (m.sg, f.sg, m.pl, f.pl) for 25 countries; link country → nationality
canDo: I can say what nationality someone is, using the correct form.
competence: Produce all 4 nationality forms for each of 25 countries; match country → nationality (≥20/25).

description: Name languages linked to 25 countries; use on parle ___
canDo: I can say which language(s) are spoken in a given country.
competence: Match each of 25 countries to its language(s) (≥20/25).

description: Read/say 20–69; recognise 6 tens; produce composites (21,31…69) with et un where applicable
canDo: I can understand and say numbers from 20 to 69 in simple exchanges (ages, prices, quantities).
competence: Read aloud any number 20–69; identify the 6 tens; build composites 21–69 with et un where required (≥90%).

description: Conjugate avoir; express age (J'ai ___ ans) and states (faim, soif, chaud, froid); distinguish être (triste, fatigué, content) vs avoir; affirmative and negative forms
canDo: I can say my age and how I feel, in the affirmative and the negative.
competence: Conjugate avoir (≥7/8); give age (J'ai ___ ans); express the 4 states; sort 6 states into être vs avoir (≥5/6); produce affirmative and negative forms.

description: Write 3–4 sentences presenting a francophone country (name, location, language, one cultural fact)
canDo: I can write a few simple sentences about a francophone country I know, if I can prepare.
competence: Write 3–4 comprehensible sentences with all 4 elements present (name, location, language, one cultural fact).
fr: Un petit texte sur un pays

topic: Everyday objects — c'est un… / ce sont des…
description: Identify and present objects/people using c'est + un/une + N and ce sont + des + N; ask C'est quoi ?
canDo: I can point out and name objects and people and ask what something is.
competence: Present ≥6 of the 14 items (un sac, un livre, un cahier, un téléphone, un stylo, un crayon, un passeport, une carte d'identité, une trousse, des ciseaux, une gomme, un portefeuille, des lunettes, une clé) with c'est + un/une and ce sont + des; ask C'est quoi ?

description: Use possessive adjectives mon/ma/mes, ton/ta/tes, son/sa/ses, notre/votre/leur/leurs; apply correct form based on gender and number of the noun (not the owner)
canDo: I can say what belongs to me and to others.
competence: Select the correct possessive (mon/ma/mes … son/sa/ses, + notre/votre/leur) by the noun's gender/number for ≥8 prompts (≥80%).

description: Express likes using aimer + definite article + N (J'aime le cinéma) and aimer + infinitive (J'aime lire); conjugate across all persons
canDo: I can say what things and activities I like.
competence: Conjugate aimer in all persons; produce aimer + definite article + N and aimer + infinitive (≥2 each).

description: Say what one does using faire + du/de la/de l'/des; produce the correct article contraction (faire du sport, faire de la natation, faire de l'équitation, faire des randonnées)
canDo: I can say what sports and activities I do.
competence: Produce faire + du/de la/de l'/des with the correct contraction for ≥6 activities (≥80%).

description: Ask and answer why: Pourquoi ? → parce que c'est + adjective or parce que j'aime + N
canDo: I can ask why and give a simple reason for a preference.
competence: Answer Pourquoi ? with parce que c'est + adjective or parce que j'aime + N for ≥3 prompts.

description: Say where one goes using aller + au/à la/à l'/aux; correct article contraction (aller au cinéma, à la plage, à l'école, aux magasins)
canDo: I can say where I go.
competence: Produce aller + au/à la/à l'/aux with the correct contraction for ≥6 destinations (≥80%).

description: Say when one does something: le lundi, le week-end, tous les jours/soirs/matins, à + time (à 8 heures, à midi, à minuit)
canDo: I can say when I do my regular activities.
competence: Use le + day, le week-end, tous les…, and à + time for ≥5 prompts; sort into day/frequency/clock.

topic: Négation — pas de ou pas le ?
description: Use ne … pas with the right article family: pas de/d' after faire, il y a and quantities (Je ne fais pas de tennis. / Il n'y a pas d'eau.), but keep le/la/les after aimer, adorer, détester (Je n'aime pas le tennis.)
canDo: I can say what I don't do and what I don't like.
competence: use ne … pas de after faire/il y a and quantities, but keep le/la/les after aimer, adorer and détester

description: Use vouloir to invite (Tu veux venir ?), accept (Je veux bien !), refuse (Je ne peux pas), reschedule (On peut se voir samedi ?)
canDo: I can invite someone and accept, refuse, or suggest another time, using set phrases.
competence: Use vouloir/pouvoir to perform all 4 functions (inviter/accepter/refuser/reporter) in a short dialogue.

topic: Well wishes + connectors for a short email
description: Produce well-wish formulas (Bon anniversaire!, Bonne chance!, Bon voyage!, Bonne année!, Bonne fête!); use connectors in a short holiday email (d'abord, ensuite, aussi, mais, et, enfin)
canDo: I can write a short, friendly message with good wishes and simple linking words, if I can prepare.
competence: Produce well-wish formulas; write a 4–6 sentence email using ≥3 connectors (d'abord/ensuite/aussi/mais/et/enfin) correctly.

description: Describe weather: Il fait beau/chaud/froid/mauvais, il pleut, il neige, il y a du vent/du soleil/des nuages; ask Quel temps fait-il ?
canDo: I can talk about and ask about today's weather in simple terms.
competence: Describe the weather with ≥6 expressions (≥80%); ask Quel temps fait-il ?

topic: en / au / aux / à — prepositions for cities & countries
description: Use en/au/aux/à with être, aller, venir for location and movement (Je suis en France. / Je vais au Japon. / Elle vient des États-Unis.)
canDo: I can say which country I am in, going to, or coming from.
competence: Use en/au/aux/à with être/aller/venir in ≥6 sentences (≥80%).

description: Use être/aller/venir + article contraction for town places (Je suis au café. / Je vais à la pharmacie. / Il vient du marché.)
canDo: I can say where I am, where I am going, and where I am coming from around town.
competence: Use être/aller/venir + contraction (au/à la/à l'/aux, du/de la/de l') in ≥6 sentences (≥80%).
fr: Il y a quoi en ville ?

description: Locate places using spatial prepositions + article contraction: à côté du/de la/de l', en face du/de la, près du/de la, loin du/de la
canDo: I can say where a place is in relation to another one.
competence: Use the spatial prepositions (à côté de, en face de, près de, loin de) + correct contraction for ≥4 prompts.

description: Form yes/no questions with Est-ce que…? and intonation; form open-ended questions with Où, Quand, Comment, Pourquoi, Qu'est-ce que, Qui, Combien de
canDo: I can ask simple yes/no and open questions to get the information I need.
competence: Form a yes/no question with Est-ce que…?; form an open question with each of the 7 question words (≥80%).

description: Ask for and give directions without the imperative, producing vous + present and c'est + preposition (Vous allez tout droit. / Vous tournez à gauche. / Vous prenez la première rue à droite. / C'est au bout de la rue.), and understanding the il faut + infinitive and on + present variants met in the reading texts; use the ordinals première and deuxième in street directions
canDo: I can ask for and give simple directions to a place, without using commands.
competence: Give directions with vous + present / c'est + preposition (no imperative), understanding il faut + infinitive / on + present variants; use the ordinals première and deuxième correctly in ≥4 prompts (≥80%).

topic: pouvoir — what one can do (+ where)
description: Use pouvoir + infinitive for possibility and permission; conjugate across key persons; say what can be done in a place (On peut visiter le musée. / Je peux manger ici ? / Vous pouvez vous garer ici.)
canDo: I can say what is possible or allowed in a place and ask for permission.
competence: Conjugate pouvoir (key persons); produce ≥3 on peut / je peux / vous pouvez + infinitive statements.

topic: Getting around — en train, à vélo (+ y)
description: Ask how one gets somewhere (Comment tu vas à l'école ?); answer with prendre + mode of transport; use pronoun y (J'y vais en bus. / On y va ? / Je prends le métro.)
canDo: I can ask how someone travels somewhere and say how I get there.
competence: Ask Comment tu vas à…?; answer with prendre + transport; use the pronoun y in ≥3 sentences.

description: Express wants and needs using je voudrais, j'aimerais, j'ai envie de, j'ai besoin de, je veux + noun or infinitive
canDo: I can express what I want and need politely.
competence: Use je voudrais / j'aimerais / j'ai besoin de / je veux + noun or infinitive (all 4).

description: Describe the steps for arriving somewhere using d'abord, puis, ensuite, après, enfin/finalement, giving each step in the present tense with an explicit subject (D'abord, tu prends la première rue à droite. Ensuite, tu vas tout droit. — no imperative); combine with transport and direction vocabulary
canDo: I can explain step by step how to get somewhere, linking the steps in order.
competence: Describe ≥4 ordered steps using d'abord/puis/ensuite/après/enfin, each step in the present tense with an explicit subject (no imperative), with transport + direction vocabulary.

description: Name meals (petit-déjeuner, déjeuner, goûter, dîner) and common foods/drinks at each; say what one eats/drinks
canDo: I can say what I eat and drink at each meal.
competence: Name the 4 meals and ≥2 foods/drinks each; say what I eat/drink (≥80%).

description: Distinguish liking (J'aime le pain — défini) from consuming (Je mange du pain — partitif); use du/de la/de l'/des with food verbs; switch to de/d' after a negative (Je ne mange pas de viande. / Il ne boit pas d'alcool.); conjugate manger and boire across all persons
canDo: I can talk about what I eat and drink — and what I don't — using the right articles.
competence: Choose definite vs partitive correctly in ≥8 prompts (≥80%); rewrite ≥5 negatives with de/d'; conjugate manger and boire (≥7/8 each).

description: Describe habits using toujours, souvent, parfois, rarement, (ne…) jamais; place adverb correctly after the verb
canDo: I can say how often I do everyday things.
competence: Place the 5 frequency adverbs correctly relative to the verb in ≥5 sentences; order them on a frequency scale.

topic: Commerces — shopping, and the market exchange
description: Identify food shops (boulangerie, épicerie, boucherie, marché, supermarché); say where one shops; ask Combien ça coûte ? / Je voudrais ___, s'il vous plaît. Play both sides of a market exchange and know who says what: Je voudrais 2 kilos de pommes de terre. / Et avec ceci ? / Ça fait combien ? / C'est tout, merci ! / Ça fait 5,89 €.
canDo: I can shop for food, ask the price, ask for what I want politely, and handle a simple market exchange on either side of the stall.
competence: Match ≥5 shops to what they sell; say where I shop; ask Combien ça coûte ? / Je voudrais ___, s'il vous plaît; assign each line of a market dialogue to le marchand or le client, put the exchange in order, and produce Je voudrais…, Ça fait combien ?, Et avec ceci ?

description: Understand and produce the numbers 70–99 — the soixante-dix and quatre-vingt system needed to handle real market prices: Ça fait quatre-vingt-cinq euros.
canDo: I can say and understand the numbers from 70 to 99, including in prices.
competence: Count 70–99 following the soixante-dix / quatre-vingts patterns, and use them in market prices (Ça fait … euros).

description: Use ce/cet/cette/ces; apply correct form by gender and number (ce pain, cet ananas, cette tarte, ces légumes)
canDo: I can point out specific items (this/these) when shopping or ordering.
competence: Select ce/cet/cette/ces correctly by gender/number for ≥8 nouns (≥80%).

description: Talk about plans with the futur proche: aller + infinitive across all persons (Je vais manger. / Nous allons visiter le marché.); say what you are going to do today, this weekend, after class
canDo: I can say what I am going to do.
competence: Produce ≥5 futur-proche sentences with correctly conjugated aller + infinitive.

description: Give simple advice with tu dois + inf (personal obligation), il faut + inf (general necessity) and tu peux + inf (suggestion): Tu dois dormir plus. / Il faut manger des légumes. / Tu peux prendre le bus.
canDo: I can give simple advice about food, health and daily life.
competence: Give ≥5 pieces of advice using devoir/falloir/pouvoir + infinitive with correct forms.

description: Give a simple restaurant review with positive and negative points (C'est délicieux ! / Le service est lent. / C'est trop cher mais c'est bon. / Je recommande / Je ne recommande pas.)
canDo: I can give a simple opinion about a restaurant, mentioning good and bad points.
competence: State ≥1 positive point, ≥1 negative point, and a clear recommendation (Je recommande / Je ne recommande pas).

description: Role-play a complete restaurant interaction: greet the waiter, read the menu, order (entrée/plat/boisson/dessert), interact during the meal, ask for the bill, pay and say goodbye
canDo: I can get by in a simple restaurant visit from arrival to paying, using set phrases, as long as staff are patient.
competence: Complete all 6 steps: greet, read the menu, order (entrée/plat/boisson/dessert), interact, ask for the bill, pay and say goodbye.
